messages:
anya: Quick triage — we have a pile of customer asks around the embeddings API: batching limits, dims (1024/2048/4096), model selection, and response format. Need to lock launch scope + acceptance criteria by EOD Friday.

mike: Can we do variable dims per model (i.e., response dim depends on model)?

sophia: Yes, models have fixed output dims. API should surface the dimension for each model. But we need to decide which dims we expose at launch.

sam: Performance note: 4096 dims ~2x memory + network compared to 2048. On hosted infra, large dims push batching down. Current safe max_batch for hosted is ~256 items @ 2048 before latency regresses. Dedicated can go higher but depends on pool size.

anya: Proposal for launch tiers:
- MVP Hosted: 1024 and 1536 models (cover most PLG customers)
- Dedicated: 2048 and 4096 available behind reserved capacity (opt-in)
- Default API behavior: model determines dims; clients can request "model": "text-emb-3-small" or "text-emb-3-large"

mike: Sounds reasonable. For payload: customers asking for compressed/packed embeddings (proto/binary or base64). Do we support alt encodings at launch?

sophia: We should start with canonical JSON array of floats for simplicity. Add optional base64-encoded float32 blob as an opt-in header later. That reduces initial complexity for SDKs and debugging.

anya: Agreed. MVP response shape suggestion (simple):
```json
{
  "model": "text-emb-3-small",
  "dimension": 1536,
  "data": [
    {"id":"item-1","embedding": [0.001, -0.23, ...]},
    {"id":"item-2","embedding": [0.11, 0.05, ...]}
  ]
}
```
(we'll document streaming and compressed payloads as "opt-ins" for Dedicated later)

sam: Important: include per-item `id` echo and `metadata` passthrough. Also include `model_hash` or `checkpoint` so customers can verify exact model.

mike: Agree on `id` echo and `model` + `dimension`. For large batches we should also return per-item processing time in ms to help customers estimate cost.

anya: Launch acceptance criteria (draft):
- API supports batch up to 256 items for hosted (1024/1536) with 95th-percentile single-call latency <= 350ms for 1-item and <= 1.2s for 128-item median.
- Dedicated: support 512+ batch and 4096 dims with documented capacity/latency SLAs.
- SDKs: Python + JS preview with examples and schema validation.
- Response format: canonical JSON array, per-item id echo, model, dimension, and optional metadata echo.

sophia: We need concrete perf targets from infra. Sam, can you validate the latency numbers above with a perf run by tomorrow?

sam: Will run microbenchmarks on current infra VM (g5-std) and dedicated test pool. Expect to have numbers tomorrow AM. ops-bot: perf-job queued (#emb-perf-191111).

mike: Question: batching semantics — do we allow different inputs lengths in same request? Many customers will send mixed-length texts.

sophia: Yes. Runtime supports per-item tokenization and dynamic batching. We just need to document cost implications (longer inputs increase runtime and may reduce effective throughput).

anya: Customer asks: A few pilot customers want 4096 dims in Hosted (no dedicated). We should push back: 4096 will be expensive and may affect other tenants. Proposal: offer a "high-dim pilot" with capacity gating + rate limits; convert to paid dedicated after pilot.

mike: +1. We can offer throttled access via feature flag and per-customer quotas.

sam: Implementation note: the routing layer needs a policy: if host_capacity < threshold, fallback to 1536 model or fail-fast with clear error. We should avoid silent degradation.

sophia: Also add a quality/regression gate: embeddings similarity A/B test against baseline on our eval set before enabling any high-dim model to customers.

anya: Action items: 
- @sam: perf runs and confirm batch limits + latency numbers (due: tomorrow 10am)
- @sophia: finalize model list (text-emb-3-small/large + hashes) and eval checklist (due: Thu)
- @mike: draft API schema + example payloads for SDKs (due: Thu)
- @anya: write launch acceptance doc and customer communication draft (due: Fri)

mike: I'll put the schema in a short PR and tag you all.

ops-bot: Added action items to backlog (#ENG-emb-launch)

anya: One more thing — must decide default rate limits per project for embeddings heavy use. Let's sync w/ growth on quota numbers after perf results. :thumbsup:

sophia: ack

sam: ack

mike: ack :rocket:
